## Goal

Fix gh-80: a conflict resolved in `merge` (by merging the story branch into the slice) stays resolved when integrate runs again. Repro as a passing regression test.

## Progress

- Fix direction picked: integrate keeps the merge (the first direction in story.md's Wanted). `rebase()` in `packages/adapters/src/git/index.ts` now runs `git rebase --rebase-merges <onto>` (W2 rebase + fast-forward, W4 conflict_loop not spent twice on one conflict). This is the smallest change, and it also covers a merge made by a person. Trade-off: once a slice merged the story branch, the history integrated onto the story branch is not linear.
- Port doc in `packages/core/src/ports.ts` says rebase keeps merge commits.
- Regression test at seam 1: `packages/cli/test/integrate.test.ts` "conflict resolved by merging the story branch stays resolved (gh-80)". It was red before the fix (conflict) and is green after. The evidence harness loop (seam 2) is green with the fix too, run as a throwaway copy and not committed: the fix is in the adapter, so the unit seam catches it.
- The e2e effect transcript was rewritten (`NORN_TRANSCRIPT_UPDATE=1`). The diff is only `git rebase` → `git rebase --rebase-merges` (2 lines).
- typecheck green. Full suite: one failure was the transcript (now updated). `cockpit.test.ts` CP6 failed once under full-suite load (50 ms timer) and passes alone: a timing flake, not related.
- Not changed (out of scope, noted for a person): the norn-merge skill still says "merge by default", and the GR4/BS4 wording was left as it is.
- implement#1 done: integrate's rebase now uses --rebase-merges (adapters git rebase), so a conflict merge resolved with git merge --no-ff stays resolved (W2, W4). Regression test in integrate.test.ts: red before, green after. The evidence harness loop is green. e2e transcript updated (rebase args only). typecheck green; full suite green apart from a cockpit CP6 timing flake that passes alone.
- review#1: changes requested (1 blocking, spec). --rebase-merges keeps the resolution only while the story branch stays put. If the story branch gets any commit between the merge step and the next integrate, the rebase re-creates the merge (`merge -C`) onto the new tip and the same conflict comes back (repro in plain git in the findings). integrate.test.ts 11/11 and typecheck green.
- review#1 changes_requested: Blocking F1: --rebase-merges only fixes gh-80 while the story branch has not moved. If the story branch advances before integrate runs again, the merge is re-created and the same conflict comes back (repro in findings). Standards clean, tests and typecheck green.

## Resume

Rework F1 in the review findings: integrate must not redo a merge the slice already made, even after the story branch has moved on (for example, merge the story branch in instead of rebasing when the slice already merged it). Add a regression test where the story branch gets an unrelated commit between the merge step and the second integrate.
